recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Re-adding a separate suspended code to CarePlan.status would conflict with the current shared request-status terminology and later workflow corrections.
issue_request: FHIR-11172 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request from the DSTU2 ballot asking for CarePlan.status to include a suspended state for temporarily paused care plans.
initial_application: The request was historically applied in commit f39dde8e171836d3345715f788c746e0a1624492, whose subject explicitly says it added suspended to the CarePlan status value set for #11172.
additional_context: CarePlan was later aligned with the workflow Request pattern through the Patient Care workflow family. The current request-status code system uses on-hold rather than suspended for the temporary-withdrawal/resume-in-future concept, and FHIR-26677 plus implementer discussion confirmed that the required request-status value set is authoritative over stale short descriptions.
reconciliation: No source change was made. CarePlan is active in source/fhir.ini, CarePlan.status is required-bound to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/request-status, and request-status.on-hold preserves the suspended semantics requested by the issue.

related_jiras.note: The seed comment cites the old tracker for Patient Care following workflow; it is a duplicate/workflow-alignment issue and is already represented on the combined branch.
Broader Patient Care workflow standardization kept CarePlan aligned with the Request pattern.
Published R5 technical correction confirmed request-status uses on-hold/revoked and aligned Request.status prose with the value set.
